intro_commit_message: lavc: add a ProRes RAW decoder
fix_commit_message:
avcodec/prores_raw: Fix heap buffer overflow

When dimensions differ from context, those were updated using
ff_set_dimensions, however this overwrote the aligned coded_width and
coded_height that were set before, leading to a buffer overflow when
writing the frame data.

Fixes: OssFuzz 438771336
Fixes: Heap-buffer-overflow

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Marvin Scholz <epirat07@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Marvin Scholz <epirat07@gmail.com>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix c9e93df4eed9 on top of intro 589b3ed943d4 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): The ProRes RAW decoder (libavcodec/prores_raw.c), added in commit 589b3ed943, computed the 16-byte-aligned coded_width/coded_height for the decoded frame before calling ff_set_dimensions() to update avctx->width/height when the stream's resolution changes. ff_set_dimensions() internally also sets avctx->coded_width/coded_height (to the unaligned width/height), so calling it after the manual alignment assignment caused the aligned values to be discarded/overwritten with unaligned ones. Downstream code that allocates or writes to the frame buffer relies on coded_width/coded_height being 16-aligned, so when the actual width/height is not a multiple of 16 the buffer ends up undersized relative to what is written, causing a heap buffer overflow. This was found via OSS-Fuzz (case 438771336) and fixed in c9e93df4eed93fe0044c52d953688c4180de1d48 by simply reordering the two code blocks so the alignment assignment happens after ff_set_dimensions(). Root cause: Incorrect ordering of two dimension-setting operations: the aligned coded_width/coded_height assignment happened before a call to ff_set_dimensions(), which itself also assigns (unaligned) values to those same fields, silently overwriting the alignment performed just before it.
